ledger.claim: The contact obligation in POL-NS-23 has two limbs — a message and a call — and only the message limb is met on this record. The driver did send two in-app messages at 10:17:20 and 10:20:45, but the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty and there is no voice-call entry anywhere in the chat log, so no in-app call was placed to the rider before the 10:23:30 cancellation. The derived contact_before_cancel block records call_count 0, an empty calls array, and obligation_met false. The rider's account that 'He never called me' is exactly what the platform's own call list shows. POL-NS-23 provides that if either limb is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged, so the 5.00 SGD fee fails on this ground alone.

POL-NS-23 is conjunctive — 'at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call'. Two messages, however timely, cannot supply the missing call, and the driver's own claim text ('messaged and called the passenger two times') is simply not borne out by the call record. Nor does anything turn on when the rider opened those messages: even reading the read receipts at their worst against the rider (10:17:33 and 10:21:22, both before the 10:23:30 cancellation), the limb that failed is the call, not the reading of a message.

Because the contact obligation failed, POL-NS-23 does not merely withhold the fee — it voids it 'with no driver compensation'. POL-NS-22 cannot rescue the driver's claim either: the 5.00 SGD is transferred to the driver as compensation only '[w]hen the driver cancels after the free wait', and that entitlement presupposes a fee that stands, which POL-NS-23 has already removed. The driver's request for the money must therefore be refused twice over.

The driver, not the rider, filed this dispute, and the ledger already sits where the rider says it should: EV-FARE-05062 records refund_issued_sgd 5.00 against total_charged 5.00 with payment_status REFUNDED, and the trip record shows the fee_reversed event at 11:56:30 that refunded the rider and withheld the amount from the driver. There is nothing left to refund and nothing left to collect; what the driver asks is a reversal of that reversal. Under POL-GEN-03 the driver's unsupported claim leaves the present state standing — the filing party's claim is not supported and no amount is moved — and the rider carries nothing. Put the other way, as the voiding rule expresses it, the fee charged is not collected from the rider and no compensation goes to the driver; the money result is the same either way.

The rider does not contest the arrival or the length of the wait. EV-GPS-05062's arrival check corroborates the 10:17:00 arrival with the nearest fix 5.75 m from the pickup at 10:17:11, and the 10:23:30 cancellation is 390 s after arrival, past POL-NS-21's 300 s free wait. That concession does not save the fee, because the wait and the charge sit downstream of the contact obligation: POL-NS-21 permits a cancellation as a rider no-show only after the free wait, and POL-NS-22 charges the fee only '[w]hen the driver cancels after the free wait' — neither clause dispenses with POL-NS-23's message-and-call requirement. A driver who waits the full five minutes and then cancels without ever calling is still outside the clause, and waiting longer cannot cure a limb the driver never performed.

Absence is citable, and here it cuts nowhere in the driver's favour. The only artifact in this case that is not complete is the traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-05062-01: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact, and this one bears on neither the contact obligation nor the timing of the wait. It cannot be used to convert a call-less cancellation into a chargeable no-show, and no other artifact in the case is impaired: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown all stand at weight 1.0.

No fraud flag is recorded for either party — the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 0 — and the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ordinary standard applies and per POL-NS-26 the ruling on this no-show is final (the fee is fixed at 5.00 SGD). There is no open fact here of the kind that sends a case to human review: the contact obligation is established from the platform's own call list and chat log, and the one missing artifact carries no fact. The rider is entitled to have the voiding of the fee confirmed now, not deferred.

The driver was physically at the pickup when he marked arrival. The GPS trace's nearest fix to the pickup point is 5.75 m away at 10:17:11 with a reported horizontal accuracy of 4 m — inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — so the 10:17:00 arrival event is corroborated by the trace and the arrival test in the no-show policy is satisfied.

The driver served the whole free wait and more. The wait ran from his 10:17:00 arrival, the 300 s free wait expired at 10:22:00, and he did not cancel until 10:23:30 — 390 s after arrival, with cancelled_after_free_wait recorded as true. The cancellation therefore came after the free wait had expired, which is exactly when POL-NS-21 allows a driver to cancel as a rider no-show.

The sum the driver asks for is the fee the schedule fixes and nothing more: the payments ledger carries one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy is true, and driver_compensation_if_upheld is 5.00 SGD, so the figure POL-NS-22 would move is 5.00 SGD with no adjustment.

The message limb of the driver's contact obligation is satisfied on the record: the chat log shows two in-app messages from the driver, sent at 10:17:20 and 10:20:45, both before the 10:23:30 cancellation, and the trip record's chat_message_count of 2 matches the log.

The rider had actual notice and her account should be discounted. Both messages were delivered at 10:17:22 and 10:20:47 and read at 10:17:33 and 10:21:22 — every one of those times before the 10:23:30 cancellation — and the platform pushed 'Your driver has arrived' to her at 10:17:04. Her statement that she 'only saw his messages after he cancelled' is contradicted by the read receipts in the chat log.

The 5.00 SGD was taken off the driver on a complaint, not on a finding. The trip record logs the 11:56:30 event as an 'interim reversal after a rider complaint ... pending review', so the present state is provisional; the merits of the no-show are being decided for the first time here and are read from the record under POL-GEN-03.

The driver does not press the assertion in his own claim that he 'called the passenger two times'. The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry, so the call limb of POL-NS-23 is not evidenced on this record and no call is asserted. The driver puts his case on the limbs the record does show: a corroborated arrival at the pickup, a full free wait observed to 390 s, and two in-app messages that the rider read before he cancelled.

No escalation threshold is engaged on this record: the driver profile carries fraud_flags 0 and the rider profile carries no fraud flag (0 when absent), and the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the driver's claim is to be decided finally on this record rather than held.

ruling.explanation:
Summary for both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was correctly reversed, and because the driver filed this dispute, the present state stands. Nothing moves in either direction.

What is not in dispute. The driver arrived at the pickup (Block 210, Tampines Street 23) at 10:17:00, and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix is 5.75 m from the pickup at 10:17:11 with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. He then observed the full 300-second free wait, which expired at 10:22:00, and did not cancel until 10:23:30 — 390 seconds after arrival, with cancelled_after_free_wait true. The arrival and the wait satisfy POL-NS-21, and the fee on the record is exactly the policy's 5.00 SGD (fee_matches_policy true), so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire.

Why the charge still fails. POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) requires the driver, before cancelling for a no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before the cancellation. The message limb is met — two messages sent at 10:17:20 and 10:20:45, both before 10:23:30. The call limb is not: the trip record's in-app call list is empty (call_count 0), there is no voice-call entry in the chat log, and the derived contact block records obligation_met false. The driver's filing says he 'called the passenger two times', but nothing in the record supports it and the driver's own submissions do not press it. Where either limb is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation. POL-NS-22 cannot rescue the charge, because its entitlement to the 5.00 SGD presupposes a fee that stands, and on this record none does.

The money. EV-FARE-05062 shows a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, total_charged 5.00 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 5.00 SGD and payment_status REFUNDED, and the trip record shows the fee_reversed event at 11:56:30 that returned the 5.00 SGD to the rider and withheld it from the driver. The rider is owed that refund, so your claim fails, driver, and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with both amount fields null.

The remaining points. The read receipts do not change anything — even taken at their strongest against the rider (read at 10:17:33 and 10:21:22), the limb that failed is the call, not the reading of a message. That the reversal was logged 'pending review' only means this is the first decision on the merits, which are as set out above. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05062-01 is missing (weight 0.0) and, under POL-GEN-02(3), carries no fact; it bears on neither the contact obligation nor the timing of the wait, and no fact this decision needs is left unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. No fraud flag is present on either profile and the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so per POL-NS-26 this AI ruling is final.

Referrals: none. The fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so the POL-NS-22 amount-check referral does not fire; the rider profile does not carry the no_show_cancellations_30d counter that POL-NS-25 requires (the rule applies only when that field is present); and POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is a remedy for a driver no-show, which did not happen here because the driver arrived.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
